host_note: Host: Escherichia coli. Membrane predictions refer to a generic membrane context (cytoplasmic vs non-cytoplasmic side); no specific host membrane is assigned, and these are not viral-envelope predictions.
coordinate_convention: 1-based inclusive amino-acid positions in the annotated precursor translation
segment_encoding: comma-separated LABELstart-stop runs (1-based inclusive) covering every residue exactly once; expand to obtain the per-residue label string

state_definitions.I: inside / cytoplasmic side of the membrane (model-defined)
state_definitions.O: outside / non-cytoplasmic side (model-defined). In DeepTMHMM beta-barrel (BETA) predictions, O is the extracellular side of the outer membrane and P is the periplasm; alpha-helical models do not split periplasm from exterior
state_definitions.S: signal peptide (precursor numbering; predicted, cleavage not demonstrated)

proteins.note: gene 0.3, inhibits EcoB and EcoK host restriction
The T7 seryl-threonyl protein kinase gp0.7 is involved in host transcription shutoff and Col Ib exclusion. Phosphorylates E. coli RNA polymerase. Other names: gp0.7.
A family of single subunit RNA polymerases.

proteins.product: dGTPase inhibitor; target for F exclusion
proteins.note: inhibits activity of the host dGTPase [dgt]. Essential only in strains that overexpress dGTPase [optA1 mutation]. In T7, gp1.2 also causes F plasmid exclusion. In T3, however, gp1.2 overcomes the exclusion system. Other names: dGTP triphosphohydrolase inhibitor; gp1.2.
Catalyzes the ATP-dependent formation of a phosphodiester bond at the site of single-stranded breaks in double-stranded DNA. T7 ligase is essential in ligase-deficient hosts only.
not essential in T7. Other names: gp1.8

T7 RNA polymerase inhibitor binds to host RNA pol and suppresses its activity on a subset of promoters. gp2 deficient T7 display reduced DNA replication and premature breakdown of replicating DNA, specifically at the left end of the genome, along with the presence of empty proheads. Rifampin can compensate for the missing gp2 function. Other names: gp2.

proteins.product: Gp2.5-like ssDNA binding protein and ssDNA annealing protein
proteins.note: binds single-stranded DNA. In phage T7 gp2.5 is essential for DNA replication and recombination. Other names: gp2.5; SSB.

T7 endonuclease I is a Holliday junction resolvase encoded by T7 gene 3. Mutants in gene 3 are defective in recombination and accumulate branched DNA. Endonuclease I may also play a role in the degradation of the host genome following infection with T7.

T7 lysozyme hydrolyzes an amide bond in the host cell wall following its release from the cytoplasm. In addition, T7 lysozyme inhibits T7 RNA polymerase initiation. This inhibition is greater for class II promoters than class III promoters and therefore may aid in temporal regulation of transcription and the switch to particle assembly. In T7, lysozyme, unlike the T7 holin, is expressed with and lies in the same region as the replication genes. Lack of gp3.5 reduces replication and burst size and delays, but does not completely prevent lysis. Mutations in the muralytic domain of gene 16, an inner capsid protein, can partially compensate for a deletion of gp3.5. Other names: gp3.5; amidase; N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanine amidase
not essential in T7; Other names: gp4.3.
not essential in T7. Other names: gp4.5.

in Enterobacteria phage T7, gp5.5 abolishes E. coli nucleoid protein H-NS-mediated inhibition of transcription by T7 RNA polymerases in vitro. Not essential, but mutants have lower burst size. Mutants in this gene are not capable of replicating in phage lambda lysogens. Other names: gp5.5
not essential. Other names: gp5.9; exonuclease V inhibitor

The T7 exonuclease encoded by gene 6 is required for (a) recombination and (b) for the degradation of host chromosomal DNA. The latter process provides nucleotides for phage DNA replication. Both processes are carried out together with the T7 gene 3-encoded endonuclease/Holliday junction resolvase. In addition, the exonuclease also functions as an RNase H that removes RNA primers during DNA replication and promotes concatemer formation.
may be involved in virion morphogenesis and is injected from virion into host cell. Other names: gp6.7
required for virion infectivity but not morphogenesis. In T7, gp 7.3 appears to be required for the assembly of tail fibers on capsids. Other names: gp7.3
Phage T7-like scaffolding protein. The protein is encoded by gene 9 in T7 (gp9) and is required for the formation of pro-capsids.

major capsid protein. Involved in F-exclusion of wt T7 phage. A minor capsid protein (gp10B) is produced from gene 10 by a -1 frameshift towards the end of 10A, resulting in a slightly larger protein. Other names: gp10A.

major capsid protein. Involved in F-exclusion of wt T7 phage. A minor capsid protein (gp10B) is produced from gene 10 by a -1 frameshift towards the end of 10A, resulting in a slightly larger protein. Other names: gp10A.
Tail tubular proteins A and B are required for assembly of tails of T7-like phages.

Approximately 12 copies of the internal virion protein B encoded in phage T7 by gene 14 are part of the internal core of the T7 virion. Along with gp16 and gp15, the other internal core proteins, gp14 is ejected from the phage head and forms part of a putative channel that spans the entire host cell envelope and allows entry of DNA. gp14 appears to localize to the outer host membrane after ejection. Other names: gp14

Approximately 12 copies of the internal virion protein C encoded by phage T7 gene 15 (gp15) are part of the internal core of the T7 virion. Along with gp14 and gp16, the other internal core proteins, gp15 is ejected from the phage head and forms part of a putative channel that spans the entire host cell envelope and allows entry of DNA.

proteins.product: internal virion protein with endolysin domain
proteins.note: Approximately 3 copies of the internal virion protein D encoded by phage T7 gene 16 (gp16) are part of the internal core of the T7 virion. Along with gp14 and gp15, the other internal core proteins, gp16 is ejected from the phage head and forms part of a putative channel that spans the entire host cell envelope and allows entry of DNA. The N-terminus has similarity to a lytic transglycosylase and may help form a channel for phage DNA translocation through the crosslinked peptidoglycan layer of the host envelope.
in phages T7 and T3 trimers of gp17 form each of the 6 kinked tail fibers. Other names: gp17.

Type II holins have two putative transmembrane domains and are thought to allow endolysins access to the cell wall at the optimal lysis time. However, in phage T7 the holin protein gp17.5 does not appear to be essential and gp17.5 mutants only show a minor delay in lysis. Other names: gp17.5; lysis protein
involved in the packaging of genome monomers into a procapsid using head-to-tail concatemers of genomes. other names: DNA packaging protein A; DNA maturation protein A; terminase, small subunit

analog of phage lambda protein Rz, a cell lysis protein. Rz and gp18.5 share distant sequence similarity, similar function, and a similar genome neighborhood. In T7, gp18.5 interacts with gp18.7, a lambda RZ1-like lysis protein. Other names: gp18.5

in Enterobacteria phage T7, this protein interacts with gp18.5 and is expressed from the -1 frame of a gene completely overlapping gene 18.5. This suggests that it may be an analog of lambda lysis protein Rz1. Other names: gp18.7.
